description: Add comprehensive error handling to a fragile Python data fetching script located at /home/ga/workspace/data_pipeline/fetch_data.py. The script currently crashes on network errors, file errors, and JSON parsing errors. Your task: (1) Wrap API calls using 'requests.get()' in try-except blocks catching specific exceptions like requests.RequestException, requests.Timeout, requests.ConnectionError; (2) Wrap file operations using 'open()' in try-except blocks catching FileNotFoundError, IOError, PermissionError; (3) Wrap JSON parsing using 'json.loads()' in try-except blocks catching json.JSONDecodeError; (4) Add 'import logging' and configure logging, then replace print statements with logging.info/warning/error calls; (5) Include meaningful error messages with context like URLs and file paths in your exception handlers; (6) Use defensive patterns like dict.get(key, default) instead of dict[key] to avoid KeyError; (7) Ensure the script can handle at least 2 out of 3 data sources failing gracefully without crashing entirely. Do NOT use bare 'except:' clauses - always specify exception types. Save the file when complete.
